paragraphs: Rav Shisha (or Sheshet), son of Rav Idi bar Avin. Of his father, Rav Idi bar Avin, it is related in Pesachim 49a [supplied: פסחים מט.] that he married a kohen's daughter and she bore him two ordained sons [סמיכי], Rav Sheshet and Rav Yehoshua. Their father was a disciple of Rav Chisda, as explained in his entry. And Rav Shisha his son lived in the time of Abaye and Rava,

and he received [traditions] from his father, as in Taanit 13a: Rav Idi bar Avin said — Abaye said to him — Rav Shisha son of Rav Idi said: My father — this is what he found difficult. Hyman writes: And everywhere he is mentioned only by the name Rav Shisha son of Rav Idi, as in Berakhot 4a (according to the reading of דק״ס), 17a, 24a, Shabbat 114b; Pesachim 49b; 54b, 115a, Rosh Hashanah 6b, Moed Katan 11b, Yevamot

82a, Ketubot 33a, 88a, Bava Kamma 87a, Bava Batra 102b; Zevachim 14b. And sometimes he is mentioned by the name Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi, as in Shabbat 138b; Eruvin 102a, Pesachim 84b, Sukkah 53a, Bava Metzia 6a, 65a, 109a, Zevachim 6a, and Hyman reports that in almost all of these places דק״ס reads Rav Shisha. And we find in Shabbat 116b that he expounded in the name of R. Yochanan.

And in Ketubot 19b he said: 'Learn from this: מדר״ב [unresolved as supplied; the named Ketubot 19b parallel reads “from Rav Kahana”], etc.'; and in Moed Katan 14b he said: 'Thus said Shmuel.' And in Rosh Hashanah 27a he said: 'Thus said Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak.' And in Yevamot 74b he challenges the words of Rava, and Rava answered. And we likewise find that he engaged in give-and-take with ר״פ [read as Rav Papa from the following context], as in Bava Metzia

65a, 109a: he raised an objection to Rav Papa, and called him 'Mar' [Master]. And in Bava Batra 8a Rav Papa spoke to him. And in Shabbat 146a Rav Papa said: Whatever is done for adornment is permitted, as in the case of Rav Shisha son of Rav Idi, who used to adorn himself with his sheet; Hyman infers from this that he died before Rav Papa. And in Menachot 21a Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi: Thus said Rav Shisha son of Rav

This is an exact source comparison for Hyman’s compressed ש״מ מדר״ב, not an admitted expansion of the final letter or proof of the printed reading. The supplied מדר״ב and Shisha/Sheshet variants remain visible; the old Beivai suggestion stays only in historical notes.

The saved Pesachim49a paragraph supports ordained sons, not close-in-age sons, and has Rabbi Yehoshua where Hyman writes Rav Yehoshua. Hyman’s inference from past-tense adornment to death before Rav Papa remains his inference, not newly established chronology.

Fresh named digital comparisons retain occurrence-specific Shisha/Sheshet forms. Taanit 13a has Idi’s statement, Abaye’s reply and Shisha’s explanation of his father’s difficulty. Ketubot 19b names Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi and reads “from Rav Kahana”; supplied מדר״ב remains unresolved, with no admitted expansion or printed-letter repair. Moed Katan 14b offers Ameimar or, alternatively, Rav Shisha as transmitter of Shmuel’s statement; Rosh Hashanah 27a names Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak. Yevamot 74b continues onto 75a for Rava’s response. Bava Metzia 65a has Sheshet addressing Rav Papa as Mar, whereas 109a has Shisha; Bava Batra 8a places Shisha’s question before Papa’s response. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1116) gives מדר״ב in his abbreviated quotation of Ketubot 19b. The consulted Davidson text names Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi and gives “from Rav Kahana.” The abbreviation is retained as printed. Hyman’s printed references to Shabbat 146b for the teaching in Rabbi Yochanan’s name and 147a for the sheet match the consulted passages. The supplied transcription has 116b and 146a. Hyman prints Menachot 21a, and the consulted Mordechai–Ashi–Shisha exchange is on 21b. His report of the Dikdukei Soferim name readings and his inference about the order of deaths remain his.
